 Carrick expects to be in charge for next game published at 15:04 GMT 15:04 GMT 
 FT: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United boss Michael Carrick, speaking to TNT Sports: "We didn't come out, and didn't get going in the second half.
 "Half-time we could have and should have been up. Everything was positive as we hoped for. 
 "We could have made more chances. We looked in a good place and then found a way of unravelling the second half. A bad way to concede, penalty, and then we were right up against it at that moment. It turned right on its head.
 "There is no hiding from the fact that we haven't won enough games. The boys were in a good place in the first half.
 "I think we didn't start the second half particularly great. A bit scrappy and we didn't get going. They made first blow in the second half and in the end that goes on to be the difference."
 On Lisandro Martinez red card: "I have not looked at it to be honest. I have not seen it."
 On feeling let down by Martinez?: "No."
 On the fans: "There is a lot of emotion, we're a great football club, and we want to win football matches. The supporters come, make a lot of effort, pay a lot of money to watch us play. You can see from today the boys had the game in the right place and things have gone against us.
 "Things have gone against us, and gone against us in a big way. Unravelled quickly. A lot of emotion right now.
 "We have got to move forward and take the things that worked for us today. A lot of the good things, especially in the first half and use that moving forward.
 Does he think he will be in charge of the next game? "Yes."

 Can Thiago re-discover spark? published at 14:59 GMT 14:59 GMT 
 Brentford v Nottm Forest (15:00 BST) 
 Image source, Getty Images Brentford will be hoping to bounce back from their EFL Cup defeat by Sunderland on Wednesday, when they conceded three goals in a 13-minute first-spell and eventually lost 3-2.
 They did end the game on a positive note, however, with Igor Thiago scoring for the first time since mid-September.

 Forest avoiding the ghosts of past managers published at 14:57 GMT 14:57 GMT 
 Brentford v Nottingham Forest (15:00 GMT) 
 Laura Kenyon 
BBC Final Score reporter at the Gtech Community Stadium 
 The relegation zone is a scary place to lurk this Halloween. Nottingham Forest hope to claw themselves out of it when the clock strikes five, avoiding a horror story in West London. 
 Oliver Glasner's side are without a win in four league games – three defeats and failing to score in two of those. But they should take encouragement from a draw against Ipswich last time out and plenty of chances created. 
 Other Forest managers on similar poor runs have been ousted but Glasner says he feels full support from the club hierarchy. He is clearly not haunted by the ghosts of Forest's past...

 Forest in for a fright? published at 14:56 GMT 14:56 GMT 
 Brentford v Nottm Forest (15:00 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Nottingham Forest aren't big fans of Halloween.
 They've lost their last five league matches played on Halloween, a run stretching back to the first Premier League season in 1992-93 when they lost 1-0 to Ipswich.
 They do have, however, a good recent record against Brentford and won their last two games against the Bees last term.

 Can Brighton show Europe credentials? published at 14:56 GMT 14:56 GMT 
 Manchester City vs Brighton (15:00 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Brighton have been talked about as potential title contenders this season, and get a good opportunity to show their worth against current league leaders Manchester City.
 City and Brighton start the day top and third of the Premier League table respectively, but head into this one off the back of league defeats to Aston Villa and Liverpool respectively.
 If the Seagulls go one better than their 2-2 draw (after 90 minutes) at the Etihad in the EFL Cup, they will end the day just two points behind Enzo Maresca's side.
 But after beating Arsenal already this season and being among the most impressive sides in the division so far, this is a big test of their credentials and how they respond to their defeat at Anfield.

 A relegation six-pointer? published at 14:54 GMT 14:54 GMT 
 Coventry City v Sunderland (15:00 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images It is only 31 October, but is Coventry's meeting with Sunderland this afternoon a relegation six-pointer of sorts?
 The two teams start the day in 19th and 20th positions respectively and with just three league wins in 16 games combined.
 Coventry have won just once at home this season, something they must address if they are to avoid dropping back down to the Championship at the earliest possible opportunity.
 For Sunderland, they have Europa League football to manage and their squad is showing early signs of struggling to balance the regular Thursday night fixtures in between their Premier League matches.

 A rivalry stretching nearly 50 years published at 14:53 GMT 14:53 GMT 
 Coventry City v Sunderland (15:00 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images To understand why a meeting between Coventry and Sunderland has the history it does, you have to go back almost 50 years to the 1976-77 season.
 The two clubs, along with Bristol City, were locked in a relegation battle from the top-flight. 
 Sunderland's match on the final day against Everton ended in a defeat for the Black Cats and with Coventry and Bristol City's meeting with each other starting late due to traffic at the Sky Blues' then Highfield Road home.
 As the final score from Sunderland's loss was read out at Coventry, both them and the Robins petered out the remainder of their 2-2 draw with both teams settling for a point and surviving.

 Man City vs Brighton (15:00 GMT) 
 The two highest-scoring teams in the league come face to face here with Brighton notching 23 goals this season and conceding seven.
 Manchester City have conceded more (nine) and scored less (20) but with just one defeat and seven wins so far compared to the Seagulls' five wins, one draw and two losses, they enter this one with a better track record.
 City (16.7) and Brighton (16.2) are also the two highest ranked teams for expected goals so far in the top flight.

 Deja vu at the Etihad? published at 14:51 GMT 14:51 GMT 
 Manchester City vs Brighton (15:00 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images For the second time in less than 72 hours, Manchester City host Brighton. But unlike Wednesday night, this is in the Premier League and not the EFL Cup.
 Brighton took the lead twice in midweek before City replied to take the game to a penalty shootout following a 2-2 draw.
 Brighton captain Lewis Dunk was the unfortunate player to have missed the costly penalty as Man City received a favourable draw at home to League One Bradford City in the quarter-finals.
 Both teams made changes, so the identities of each side will differ. Plus no shootout today of course.
 Should be a cracker, though.

 'The mentality was there' published at 14:50 GMT 14:50 GMT 
 FT: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United 
 Manchester United 
 Man Utd forward Bryan Mbeumo, speaking to TNT Sports: 
 "A lot of disappointment. I think we have done a lot of right things, especially in the first half when we could have been up one or two-nil. 
 "I think the first half we had a lot of chances, which is a positive. The last few games we didn't create a lot, but obviously they're a good team with qualities. 
 "What we have shown today - the mentality was there. Everyone worked really hard and we still have to find some bits at the training ground. Work even harder and yes we have two very important games."
 On the players letting the manager and players down today?: "No, obviously not. I think the mentality was there right from the first minute. Harder with 10 men. We still trust everyone. With the men down, we still had some frustrations at the end. But I think we have done everything as a team today. 
 "Maybe today we just missed some chances. We could have been up early in the game, but that's a positive to take out of this game."

 'A lot of players aren't putting a shift in like they should be' published at 14:48 GMT 14:48 GMT 
 FT: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United 
 Dion Dublin 
Former Coventry and Aston Villa striker on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 I don't know how Micheal [Carrick] is doing it because it's going to be the same questions that he's going to have to answer, but in a different way. 
 I'm hoping one of the seniors comes out and explains what's going on. 
 I'm hoping someone mentions the Martinez stupidity because there comes a time where the punters need to be told something because they are travelling all over the country and at the moment they are getting no honesty, and they are getting a lot of players who aren't putting a shift in like they should be. 
 I don't think that there are many players in a Manchester United shirt right this moment who are honest with themselves and can look in the mirror and say I'm actually busting a gut every time I put a Manchester United shirt on. 
 I'm not sure there's many that can.

 'We stamped our authority' published at 14:44 GMT 14:44 GMT 
 FT: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United 
 Chelsea 
 Chelsea forward Morgan Rogers, speaking to TNT Sports : "Massive. 
 "A difficult week with a poor result last weekend. We knew we had to come out here strong. In the second half, we stamped our authority and that was really good. We deserved the win."
 On his goal: "Just to try to commit the defenders. All of a sudden, I was in on goal and had to stay composed. Luckily it went in."
 On life at Chelsea: "Loving it. A new challenge and looking forward to playing with these wonderful quality players. It is about the team coming together as a whole. Try to be a leader and stick to what I know best. A good start, but I need to keep going."
 On role today: "To try to occupy defenders in whatever space it may be. We were interchanging and doing what was necessary to occupy defenders and drag them out."
 On Cole Palmer: "Friendly competition. We always push each other in training every day. If we're both doing well and the team is doing well, that's the most important."

 By Sam Drury BBC Sport journalist Chelsea took full advantage of Manchester United's second-half collapse to condemn the visitors to a third straight loss and heap yet more pressure on Michael Carrick. 
 United are now without a win in nine games in all competitions, their longest such run since October-November 1988.
 A fourth Premier League defeat of the season leaves United 16th, a point above the relegation zone, with under-fire boss Carrick in an increasingly precarious position just days after being given the chance turn things around following a dismal start to the campaign.
 After an encouraging first-half performance, United allowed Morgan Rogers to saunter unchallenged through the heart of the defence to dink home the opener for Chelsea five minutes after the break.
 Cole Palmer doubled the hosts' lead from the penalty spot 14 minutes later after the video assistant referee spotted Lisandro Martinez, not looking at the ball, thrust an arm into the face of Wesley Fofana.
 As a result, Martinez was sent off for a second yellow card and, once Palmer converted the spot kick, the game was all but over as a contest.
 It could have been worse for the away side as Chelsea winger Estevao, handed his first league start of the season by Xabi Alonso, smashed in a third, only for it to be ruled out for a marginal offside.
 United had had the ball in the back of the net themselves during a promising first 45 minutes but Matheus Cunha's close-range header was checked by VAR and eventually disallowed for offside.
 The recalled Bruno Fernandes also put a good chance over, while Amad Diallo twice failed to convert with just Chelsea keeper Mike Penders to beat - but United failed to maintain that level in the second half.
 There had been a smattering of boos for Chelsea at half-time but they eased the displeasure with a much-improved showing after the break.
 Rogers, aided by the most generous of United defending, gave them the initial boost they needed before Martinez's two bookings in the space of three minutes, leading to Palmer's penalty, put them in complete control.
 They could, and perhaps should, have added to their advantage with the lively Estevao coming close and substitute Valentin Barco missing a glorious late chance.
 United forward Bryan Mbeumo thundered a shot against the bar in stoppage time but while Carrick's side could end the weekend in the bottom three, Chelsea are up to fourth.
 Rogers shines, 3/10 for sent-off Martinez - player ratings for Chelsea v Man Utd 
 Published 29 minutes ago 
 Have your say on Chelsea’s performance 
 What did you make of Man Utd's display? 
 Analysis: United lapses see bright start wasted 
 Going in at half-time, Carrick had every reason to be pleased with what he had seen from his side.
 They had battled well, limited Chelsea to very few chances and with more clinical finishing could have been a couple of goals ahead.
 Key to the performance was their shape and tactical discipline, giving the home side no way through.
 Yet five minutes into the second half that all went out of the window as Romeo Lavia won the ball around halfway and passed to Rogers, who must not have been able to believe his luck as the United players stood like statues as he ran towards goal.
 Andrey Santos failed to get across, while Harry Maguire and Martinez practically escorted him into the box until the forward was seven yards out and chipped into the net.
 Like that, the momentum had changed and any chance of United reversing it took a decisive hit with the Martinez red card.
 Booked for multiple kicks at Rogers' ankles just a couple of minutes earlier, the Argentina centre-back turned his back on the ball from a corner and shoved Fofana in the face.
 It was entirely needless and one of the simpler VAR decisions you'll see this season.
 The game was gone and, despite his unlikely survival this week, it would be a shock if Carrick isn't too soon.
